### PG&E Achieves 1,500-Mile Milestone in Major Wildfire Safety Undergrounding Effort


November 9, 2026


*Delivering Permanent Wildfire Risk Reduction and Greater Reliability for Customers*


OAKLAND, Calif.


, Nov. 9, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E) today announced it has reached a major wildfire safety milestone, installing and energizing 1,500 miles of underground power lines in high fire-threat districts since launching its undergrounding program in 2021.


Wildfire ignition risk on the 1,500 miles of undergrounded lines is permanently reduced by approximately 98%. Customers served by underground lines also experience approximately 90% fewer outages.


"Undergrounding is one of the most powerful tools we have to protect our customers and communities from wildfire risk. Reaching 1,500 miles is an important milestone, but what matters most is what those miles deliver: safer communities, fewer outages, and more reliable electric service over decades for the customers we're privileged to serve. We're proud of this progress and remain focused on doing this work where it can deliver the greatest safety and reliability benefits," said Matt Pender, PG&E Undergrounding and System Hardening Vice President.


The milestone comes at a critical juncture for the future of undergrounding power lines to reduce wildfire risk and improve reliability in California.


To support ongoing efforts to mitigate wildfire risk, PG&E recently filed a 10-year Electrical Undergrounding Plan (EUP) proposing to significantly reduce wildfire risk and improve reliability by undergrounding 5,000 miles of powerlines across more than 30 counties in Northern and Central California. The plan would permanently reduce wildfire risk by 98% and reduce approximately 90% of outages for customers served by those lines. It would also help prevent disruptions to hospitals, fire stations, police stations and other essential community services while reducing the need for Public Safety Power Shutoffs (PSPS) and outages associated with Enhanced Powerline Safety Settings (EPSS).


The recent California Public Utilities Commission's (CPUC) Proposed Decision (SPD-37 Joint IOU Application proceeding) could severely restrict undergrounding across California. If adopted, the Proposed Decision would reduce eligible undergrounding in PG&E's plan from 5,000 miles to approximately 1,100 miles, hindering progress on permanent wildfire risk reduction for areas with the highest wildfire vulnerability.


PG&E remains committed to advocating for permanent risk reduction in the highest wildfire-risk areas as part of its commitment to make the system safer and more reliable.


**2026 Undergrounding Progress**


As of this week, PG&E has completed 325 miles of undergrounding in 2026. In recent weeks, Foresthill (Placer County), Middletown (Lake County), Apple Hill (El Dorado County), Arnold (Calaveras County), and Angwin (Napa County) are among the numerous communities now being served by underground power lines.


**About PG&E**


Pacific Gas and Electric Co., a subsidiary of PG&E Corp. (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit pge.com and pge.com/news.
